newsitem.title: CHINA: Drought seen hitting northwest China power supply.
newsitem.headline: Drought seen hitting northwest China power supply.

text.p: Drought in northwestern China is seen hitting the region's hydroelectric output and aggravating power shortages, the China Business Times said on Thursday.

Four years of reduced rainfall along the upper reaches of the Yellow River would cut electricity generation in the northwest by 660,000 megawatt-hours between October and next May compared with October 1995 and May 1996, the newspaper said.

Water for power generation in the Longyangxia and Liujiaxia reservoirs had fallen by more than 1.2 billion cubic metres (42.4 billion cubic ft) by the end of October from the year-ago period, it said.
"This will exacerbate the electricity shortage in the northwest," it said.
Power generation from March to May next year would depend entirely on power stations on the upper reaches of the river, it quoted the Ministry of Power Industry as saying.
The Yellow River is China's second longest and powers one of the nation's major energy grids.
China has faced a chronic energy deficit as it rushes to industrialise.
